newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice 'commandos' call for separate state.
newsitem.headline: Venice 'commandos' call for separate state.

text.p: A group of men, presumed by police to be armed, who occupied the belltower in St Mark's Square in Venice on Friday said they were seeking the lagoon city's independence from Italy.

The group, believed to consist of about 10 men, issued a statement claiming to speak on behalf of the "Most Serene Government" of the lagoon city. They described themselves as a regular unit of the phantom republic's "army".
Venice was for centuries a powerful independent power. Known as the "Most Serene Republic" it came to an end on May 12, 1797 when French Napoleonic forces entered the city.
"After 200 years, a regular unit of the Most Serene Venetian Army has tonight liberated St Mark's Square," the statement, made available to an Italian state radio reporter, said.
"The Most Serene Republic of Venice has been reborn today...Long live St Mark," it said.

The statement was also heard faintly in the Venice area in a pirate radio broadcast, apparently from the belltower itself, which interrupted a state radio news bulletin. About 300 police have sealed off St Mark's Square.
